creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From tooling feedback, 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21, 0.16.2-dev on the Mac, three sightings, all Codex helpers in overnight rounds. Each ended its turn saying it would resume when its background job (a `qm` job, a background `./dev`) finished, then sat at an empty prompt with nothing running. Muster showed the pane `waiting` for 75 minutes in one case and 40 in another, so its maker heard nothing (the maker watch tells only idle), and the job's end woke nobody: Codex has nothing that starts a turn when a background process exits. One round lost about 40 minutes of its critical path.

Where the `waiting` came from is not established. A wait declared with `report --waiting` has no time limit (61045758 limits only a wait read off the screen), which would explain it; check the run log for a `report --waiting` from those panes. Declaring a wait is right for Claude Code, which a finished background task wakes, and wrong for a harness nothing wakes.

Two Codex agents tried to arrange their own wake: a watcher script that ran `muster msg post --to <itself>` when the job finished. Muster refuses that ("a post cannot be addressed to its own author").

Options, not exclusive:
- `report --waiting --until-exits <pid>`, or a `muster wake --when-exits <pid>`: the daemon ends the wait and rings the agent when the process exits.
- Limit a declared wait for a harness that a finished job cannot wake, as the screen's wait is limited, so the pane reads idle and the maker is told.
- Tell Codex agents, in its adapter's instructions, not to declare a wait nothing will end.
title: A Codex agent waiting on its own background job reads waiting for an hour, and nothing wakes it
